intro.title: This dashboard is a demonstration of the AntelopeJS DMS
intro.description: Helio, in the sidebar, is a fictional solar installer from Liège. Its whole back-office — sales pipeline, quotes, customers, catalog, projects, live service desk, team, invoices, live fleet monitoring, settings and dashboard — is built only from the DMS's generic blocks, declared in TypeScript on the backend.

pages.detail: Plus hidden detail and form pages

controllers.detail: CRUD routes generated from decorated classes

vue.detail: Every screen is made of generic blocks

helio.title: Helio, page by page
helio.description: One card per page of the Helio menu, read from the menu itself.

antelope.title: What AntelopeJS brought
antelope.description: What the framework and the DMS took care of, so that Helio only had to describe its business.

pages.title: Pages declared on the backend
pages.description: Each screen is a PageController class whose static fields are blocks: tables, forms, charts, cards. The shared frontend renders them, so Helio ships no Vue.

data.title: Data controllers
data.description: A decorated class over a table generates the list, read, create, edit, delete, export and archive routes, with the matching columns, filters and forms.

permissions.title: Permissions per block and action
permissions.description: Every page, block and action is a line of the roles editor, with no extra code: a role sees exactly what it is granted.

realtime.title: Realtime and live pages
realtime.description: The service desk and fleet monitoring refresh themselves as the backend publishes events on realtime topics.

i18n.title: Translations
i18n.description: Every text is an i18n key resolved in the reader's language: switch between English and French from the user menu.

modules.title: Feature modules
modules.description: API and database consoles, automation, SaaS billing, AI assistant, translations, page builder, media library, marketing analytics and mailing: one entry each in antelope.config.ts.

modules.title: Installed modules
modules.description: Each one adds its own pages under Modules; remove its entry in antelope.config.ts to drop it.

start.title: Getting started
start.description: From a fresh instance to your own pages.
start.builder: Edit the current page in the builder

code.title: Read the code
code.description: An excerpt of the live service desk: the page is a class, each static field a block with its options.
